answer: Mandatory cover pricing makes each fake agent pay its own premium. To register, an identity buys a policy from an underwriter, who pays 500 coins to challengers if it is proven fake. Premiums start at 5% and rise to 40% when its funding traces to the same wallet cluster, like a tide lifting every clone together. A 200-fake ferrous-grade farm in an ocean of honest agents owes about 40,000 coins in premiums, and each proven fake forfeits its policy, so cost grows per identity and cannot be pooled.
